Maximum growth rate and its timing

Source: R/maxrate.R
maxrate.Rd

Estimates the time at which growth curves grow fastest, the inflection point, the maximum growth rate there, and the fraction of the asymptote reached at that time, with standard errors by the delta method. Confidence intervals by confint: Wald, profile likelihood or parametric bootstrap intervals.

Usage

maxrate(x, curves = NULL, newdata = NULL)

Arguments

x

A gcTMB object, the result of gcTMB.

curves

Numeric matrix, list of matrices, or NULL. Linear functions to identify the parameters of the growth curves, with 5 rows (b1-b5) and one column for each model coefficient, see timeto. If curves and newdata are both NULL (default), the identity matrix, for models without covariates in fform.

newdata

Data frame or NULL. The values of the covariates in fform, one row for each growth curve, as an alternative to curves; NULL (default) to use curves.

Value

A maxrateTMB object: a list with the estimates (coef), their covariance matrix (vcov), and what confint and profile need. The estimates are named tmax, rate and fraction, followed by the name of the curve for curves from newdata or named curves, e.g. rate:trt=0.1; several unnamed curves are numbered.

Details

The curves are the population curves, with all random effects at zero; the standard errors include the uncertainty of the fixed effects. For each curve, maxrate gives

  • tmax: the time of the maximum growth rate, the inflection point of the curve;

  • rate: the maximum growth rate, the slope of the curve at tmax, in units of the response per unit of time;

  • fraction: the fraction of the asymptote b1 reached at tmax, how much of the growth has occurred when the growth is fastest.

For the logistic (Richards), hill and symmetric weibull and gompertz curves these have closed forms; for the gompertz and weibull curves with an asymmetry b5 different from 1 the inflection point is the root of an equation, see the vignette. The hill and weibull curves have an inflection point at a positive time only for b3 b5 > 1; otherwise they grow fastest at t = 0, with an unbounded rate for the hill curve, and the results are NA. The linear model grows at the constant rate b1, without an inflection point: its tmax and fraction are NA.

A truncated curve (the default of gcTMB, at b4 = 0) is the curve without truncation, f(t), shifted down to zero at its threshold b4 and rescaled, b1 (f(t) - f(b4))/(b1 - f(b4)) beyond b4. It has its maximum growth rate at the inflection point of the curve without truncation if that is after the threshold, and otherwise just after the threshold, where the slope jumps from zero: then tmax is b4 and fraction zero.

The standard errors are by the delta method, with numerical derivatives of the quantities with respect to the parameters of the curves. Profile intervals are available for tmax (by b2, unless the curve is at its threshold) and rate (by b1); for fraction, which depends on the shape of the curve only, confint returns Wald intervals with a message for method="profile".

See also

confint.maxrateTMB for confidence intervals, timeto

Examples

fit <- gcTMB(Height ~ DAS, data=FabaHeights25, model="logistic")
mr <- maxrate(fit)
mr
#> Time of the maximum growth rate (tmax), maximum growth rate (rate) and proportion of total growth at inflection (fraction):
#> 
#>          Estimate Std.Error
#> tmax       30.730   0.68220
#> rate        2.560   0.09415
#> fraction    0.454   0.00778
confint(mr, method="wald")
#>               2.5 %     97.5 %
#> tmax     29.3846302 32.0753316
#> rate      2.3743556  2.7456798
#> fraction  0.4386425  0.4693352

# the Richards curve, with an estimated asymmetry
fitr <- gcTMB(Height ~ DAS, data=FabaHeights25, fix=c(b5=FALSE), link=c(b5="log"))
maxrate(fitr)
#> Time of the maximum growth rate (tmax), maximum growth rate (rate) and proportion of total growth at inflection (fraction):
#> 
#>          Estimate Std.Error
#> tmax       30.666    3.0276
#> rate        2.560    0.0957
#> fraction    0.452    0.0854

# a curve for each treatment level
FabaHeights25$trt <- factor(FabaHeights25$Treatment)
fit2 <- gcTMB(Height ~ DAS, fform=b1 + b2 ~ trt, data=FabaHeights25)
maxrate(fit2, newdata=data.frame(trt=levels(FabaHeights25$trt)))
#> Time of the maximum growth rate (tmax), maximum growth rate (rate) and proportion of total growth at inflection (fraction):
#> 
#>                  Estimate Std.Error
#> tmax:trt=0.1       30.432   1.44817
#> rate:trt=0.1        2.441   0.10164
#> fraction:trt=0.1    0.452   0.00922
#> tmax:trt=0.3       29.080   1.42992
#> rate:trt=0.3        2.426   0.09967
#> fraction:trt=0.3    0.447   0.01029
#> tmax:trt=0.5       31.004   1.37572
#> rate:trt=0.5        2.647   0.10751
#> fraction:trt=0.5    0.454   0.00857
#> tmax:trt=0.6       31.507   1.39258
#> rate:trt=0.6        2.659   0.10806
#> fraction:trt=0.6    0.456   0.00821
#> tmax:trt=0.8       31.732   1.41979
#> rate:trt=0.8        2.604   0.10688
#> fraction:trt=0.8    0.457   0.00813
